sceneHappening: One long blessing: God's plan from before the world began, and a prayer that they know the power at work in them
summary: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through God's will, writes to the saints [in Ephesus] who are faithful in Christ Jesus: grace and peace. Then, in a single sentence in Greek, he blesses "the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ." He lists what God has done: chosen us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love; predestined us for adoption as his children through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will, to the praise of his glorious grace; in him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace which he lavished on us. He made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his purpose set forth in Christ, "to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth." In him we have obtained an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will; we who were the first to hope in Christ are to the praise of his glory. In him, you also, after hearing the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believing in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is the guarantee of our inheritance until we acquire possession of it, to the praise of his glory. For this reason Paul, hearing of their faith and love for all the saints, does not cease to give thanks for them, remembering them in his prayers, that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give them a spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him, having the eyes of their hearts enlightened, that they may know what is the hope of his calling, what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, and "what is the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe," according to the working of the strength of his might, which he worked in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places, far above all rule and authority and power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the age to come. God put all things under his feet and gave him as head over all things to the church, which is his body, "the fullness of him who fills all in all."
whySettingMatters: Several of the oldest manuscripts do not include the words "in Ephesus" in 1:1, and the letter has no personal greetings, which is why many think it began as a circular letter for several churches. Ephesus itself was a great port and religious center, famous for the temple of Artemis, and some of the language about "powers," "rulers," and "authorities" would have spoken directly to a population who feared spiritual forces and consulted magic (Acts 19:19). The opening is one long sentence of praise in the Greek, a form of Jewish blessing (berakah), and it is not an argument but a celebration of God's plan. "Chosen before the foundation of the world" and "predestined" are debated across Christian traditions: some read them as God's choice of individuals, others as God's choice of a people in Christ, and the text itself stresses that this is "in Christ" and for praise, love, and holiness. The phrase "heavenly places" appears five times in the letter and means the realm of God's rule that believers already share in Christ. The "seal" and the "guarantee" are business and legal pictures: a mark of ownership, and a down payment on the rest.

questions: Paul praises God before asking for anything. What does it say that the letter begins with blessing?
"Chosen before the foundation of the world." What does it change to know your life belongs to a plan that began before you?
Paul prays that "the eyes of your heart" would be enlightened. What kind of seeing is he talking about?
Christ is "head over all things to the church." What does it mean to say the church is "the fullness of him who fills all in all"?
